subject: Post-call: Logging controls & PII handling — next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@cardiologix.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 18:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: Logging controls & PII handling — next steps

Sam — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposal for next steps so we keep momentum on the POC.

Key points from the call (what we heard):
- Cardiologix will ingest request/response logs from your inference calls for troubleshooting and analytics; some requests include patient identifiers (PHI).
- You need the ability to: (a) redact/suppress headers containing trace IDs and cookies, (b) mask or pseudonymize request/response fields that can contain PII, and (c) control retention by workspace/route.
- Data residency requirement: US-only (US-East preferred) for production logs.

Open questions / clarifications we need from you (so we can size the engineering work):
1) Which log categories must be retained verbatim vs always masked (examples: request_path, query_params, body_payload, response_headers)?
2) Is keyed hashing (HMAC) of trace IDs acceptable if it preserves the ability to correlate a request <-> response without storing the raw trace? Or do you prefer complete removal?
3) Target retention windows per environment (dev/staging/prod) — ballpark numbers please.
4) Procurement: confirm the procurement contact and contract timeline (we can prep a standard SOW once we have procurement contact).

Proposed next steps and timeline:
- You: send the completed security questionnaire (we attached a blank version during the call).
- Redwood: run a short demo (20–30m) showing our log-redaction UI + how prefix/KV caching keeps latency while removing sensitive fields. Suggested demo window: Tue 20 Mar or Wed 21 Mar (we can do mornings PT).
- Goal: POC start within 3 weeks after questionnaire + procurement kickoff.

Attachments: redaction_design_notes.xlsx (internal sketch of options) — will share post-demo.

If that matches your view, reply with the procurement contact and whether keyed hashing is acceptable for trace IDs.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai]
[attachment: redaction_design_notes.xlsx (Excel, 42KB)]

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@cardiologix.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Logging controls & PII handling — next steps

Hannah — great summary, thanks. A few quick answers from our side:

1) Must be masked/verbatim requirements:
   - request_path: keep
   - query_params: mask any parameter values named patient_id, ssn, email, phone
   - body_payload: mask patient identifiers; we can provide two example payloads
   - response_headers: remove any cookie/session tokens; trace-id handling below

2) Keyed hashing for trace IDs is acceptable as long as:
   - the same incoming trace ID always maps to the same pseudonym within our tenant, and
   - you can provide an HMAC-based option (we'll provide a key rotation cadence requirement).

3) Retention: dev/staging = 7 days; prod = 90 days (but we may negotiate down to 30 days for some log classes if needed for cost).

4) Procurement contact: procurement@cardiologix.com (CC'd on this reply). Our legal team will want a redline of the SOW and a SOC2 report if available.

I've attached the filled questionnaire. Also attaching a redacted sample log (sample_log_redacted.json) — it's anonymized but shows the fields that will appear.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Platform Engineering — Cardiologix
[sam.patel@cardiologix.com]
[attachment: Cardiologix_Security_Questionnaire_Filled.pdf (PDF, 250KB)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 17 Mar 2028 02:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Logging controls & PII handling — next steps

Looping in Marcus for visibility on procurement/tiering. Quick internal notes and proposal:

- We can implement tenant-keyed HMAC for trace IDs without storing the raw trace token; that preserves correlation while satisfying their PHI constraints. Implementation effort: small engineering ticket + a config flag per workspace.
- Retention tiers: we will propose a configuration surface: per-route retention + route-level mask rules (UI + API). Default templates: dev=7d, staging=30d, prod=90d.
- Pricing: recommend offering a 3-month POC credit (waive some token costs) — Marcus, can we approve a $6k POC credit tied to signed SOW?

Aditya — I'll schedule the demo for Tue 20 Mar 09:30 PT unless I hear otherwise. Sam — can you confirm?

--
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- Redwood (Hannah + Engineering): prepare 20–30m demo on Tue 20 Mar 09:30 PT showing: 1) route-level mask rules in the Console, 2) tenant-keyed trace-id HMAC flow, 3) retention config per route.
- Redwood (Aditya): prep SOW draft + POC credit proposal (deal CR-5234).
- Redwood Security (Stephanie): join demo for security Q&A and to collect evidence items (SOC2, encryption at rest details).

Sam — attached is the filled questionnaire you provided; we'll inline your sample logs to the demo.

Thanks all — talk Tue.
